<text x="503.0" y="227.0" font-size="12" font-weight="400" fill="#6b7280" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="auto">and the transcript is still right</text>

<text x="830.0" y="158.0" font-size="12" font-weight="400" fill="#1f2328" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="auto">encoder self-attention has already mixed</text>
<text x="830.0" y="174.0" font-size="12" font-weight="400" fill="#1f2328" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="auto">the context into every position</text>
<text x="830.0" y="198.0" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#7c3aed" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="auto">so the decoder reads the right content</text>
<text x="830.0" y="214.0" font-size="12" font-weight="600" fill="#7c3aed" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="auto">from the “wrong” frames too</text>
<text x="830.0" y="242.0" font-size="11" font-weight="400" fill="#6b7280" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="auto">sharpness is forced only when the</text>
<text x="830.0" y="256.0" font-size="11" font-weight="400" fill="#6b7280" text-anchor="middle" dominant-baseline="auto">encoder has no context (raw log-mel)</text>
</g>
